findings.title: Streaming endpoints do not receive the contextual logger
findings.body: SubscribeStream, PublishStream and RunStream pass the original context to next without calling instrumentContext, unlike QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics. These request types also carry a PluginContext, so any logging performed downstream via a contextual logger during streaming (including long-lived RunStream handlers) will lack endpoint, pluginId, dsName/dsUID and uname, making the extracted ContextualLoggerMiddleware incomplete and its behaviour inconsistent across endpoints.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the receiver's recorded logs
findings.body: FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of returning the receiver or a logger sharing its state. LoggerMiddleware now logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx) (logger_middleware.go:58), so a test holding the original TestLogger and asserting on InfoLogs will observe zero calls even though a log was emitted; the fake therefore no longer behaves like the real logger (which writes to the same underlying output) and will silently hide the new Plugin Request Completed log in tests.

findings.title: Nil requests panic before LoggerMiddleware's nil guards can run
findings.body: QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics dereference req.PluginContext without a nil check. LoggerMiddleware explicitly guards nil requests and passes them through (logger_middleware.go:63, 77, 90, 104), but in CreateMiddlewares the contextual middleware sits in front of it (pluginsintegration.go:160-161), so a nil request now panics in this middleware instead of reaching the guarded pass-through/downstream error handling.

findings.title: No test covers contextual-logger propagation or the LoggerMiddleware field move
findings.body: The refactor removes the explicit pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname fields from LoggerMiddleware.logRequest and relies entirely on ContextualLoggerMiddleware enriching the context earlier in the chain plus Logger.FromContext honouring it, yet the only renamed test still asserts Prometheus metrics and never checks the context seen downstream or the emitted Plugin Request Completed fields. A regression in middleware ordering or in FromContext (in either the real or fake logger) that drops those log fields would pass the whole suite undetected; a chain-level test for the new middleware is needed.
